summary.title: Space Invaders from Scratch - Part 1
summary.one_liner: You learn how to open a 640x480 window with an OpenGL 3.3 core context in C++ using GLFW for windowing and GLEW for loading OpenGL functions, then run a basic game loop.
keywords: build simple arcade game from scratch
native window api cocoa x winapi
takeaways: Set a GLFW error callback, call glfwInit, then create a window with glfwCreateWindow and make its context current.
Request an OpenGL 3.3 core profile with glfwWindowHint before creating the window.
Load OpenGL functions at runtime with GLEW after the context is current, then query the GL version.
A basic game loop clears the buffer, swaps buffers, and polls events until glfwWindowShouldClose returns true.
Compile with g++ -std=c++11 linking glfw and GLEW; install glfw3 and glew via a package manager.
summary.summary: The author starts a series on building a simplified Space Invaders prototype in C++ with minimal dependencies. This first part explains why GLFW was chosen over native APIs or Qt, then walks through creating an error callback, initializing GLFW, creating a 640x480 window, setting OpenGL 3.3 core profile hints, and initializing GLEW. It ends with a minimal game loop that clears the screen to red, plus compile instructions for Linux and macOS.
